$comment: Status + body + headers → what the SDK must do. This table is the transport, and getting one row wrong is a data-loss bug: treating 503 as success drops a batch the server never stored. Actions: drop (accepted, or permanently refused: forget it) | retry (keep, back off) | split (halve and resend) | hold (pause categories) | shutdown (stop sending entirely) | degrade (change a setting, retry once).

$notes.categories: A hold starts from the endpoint's own categories: /v1/batch is ['event','identify'], /v1/errors is ['error']. X-RateLimit-Categories may narrow that set to the categories it names; it never widens it. A header naming nothing the endpoint governs is ignored, and the endpoint's categories are held.
$notes.headers: Retry-After is delta-seconds or an HTTP-date. X-RateLimit-Categories is `<seconds>:<cat>;<cat>`; when its seconds part is missing or zero, Retry-After sets the wait. With neither, the wait is the local escalating schedule.
$notes.monthly: A monthly cap holds for the server's Retry-After, but never longer than six hours at a time: a customer who upgrades mid-month starts sending again within hours instead of weeks, and one refused request every six hours costs nothing. Absent a Retry-After, hold six hours.
$notes.success: Any 2xx is an acceptance. 202 is what ingest sends; a proxy may answer 200 or 204, and treating those as failures resends accepted data.
$notes.redirects: Never follow a redirect: fetch re-sends the body and the X-Vinktar-Key header to wherever it points. A 3xx means the endpoint is misconfigured; stop sending and say so.
$notes.bodyShapes: Two 400s come from the pre-controller listener and use {"message": ...}; everything else uses {"error": ...}. Read `error ?? message`.
$notes.fields: `endpoint` defaults to /v1/batch. `wait` is seconds, or "escalating" for the local schedule. `categories` is the final held set. `source` says who produces the response: server (asserted against the real server), proxy, or network. A header value `<<now+Ns as HTTP-date>>` is rendered as the HTTP-date N seconds after the test's clock.

cases.name: accepted and durable
cases.why: 202 means durably queued in ClickHouse, not merely received. The client report carried by this request is committed here.

cases.name: accepted with per-event rejections
cases.why: A bad event never fails the batch, but the rejected one was not stored: a flush containing it is not a successful flush. Warn; do not resend, the server will reject it identically.

cases.name: accepted with traits dropped
cases.why: The identity link landed; only the named trait did not. Warn, do not retry.

cases.name: identify ignored
cases.why: The entry carried nothing to do. Surface it; retrying will be ignored identically. The codes are only what ingest can see for itself (missing_user_id, blocked_id, blocked_device_id, no_op): a refused rebind is resolved at read time and never reported here.

cases.name: accepted with suppressed occurrences
cases.why: Two occurrences matched the inbound filter: not stored, not billed. Surface the count; nothing to retry.

cases.name: accepted by a proxy with 200
cases.why: Any 2xx is an acceptance. Retrying it sends the same data twice.

cases.name: redirect
cases.why: Following it would forward the write key and the body to another origin. The endpoint is misconfigured; stop and surface it once.

cases.name: invalid gzip
cases.why: Our compression produced something the server could not inflate. Retry once uncompressed rather than losing the batch.

cases.name: invalid JSON
cases.why: Our serializer produced junk. Retrying sends the same junk. Count it as `invalid`.

cases.name: bad request
cases.why: Never retry a 4xx that is not 413 or 429.

cases.name: missing key
cases.why: A config error, not a transient one. Stop sending and stop accepting new work; surface it once. Continuing to buffer is a memory leak that never drains.

cases.name: batch too large by count
cases.why: Halve and resend. An SDK that respects maxItems should never see this.

cases.name: error batch too large by count
payload too large by bytes
cases.why: Split by bytes. A single item that still will not fit is dropped as `invalid` after shedding what it can (breadcrumbs, then source context, then frames).

cases.name: rate limited
cases.why: Hold ONLY this endpoint's categories; a throttled analytics batch must never stall an error report.

cases.name: category header cannot widen the hold
cases.why: A batch response cannot pause error reporting.

cases.name: category header without seconds
cases.why: A missing seconds part is not a zero wait; Retry-After still applies.

cases.name: auth rate limited
cases.why: Per-IP, before the key is resolved, so the server names no category. Hold the endpoint's.

cases.name: monthly cap reached, reset weeks away
cases.why: Hold at most six hours at a time: an upgrade mid-month should resume sending within hours. Tell the developer once.

cases.name: monthly cap reached, reset within the hour
cases.why: Holding six hours past a reset that is forty minutes away loses nothing but delays everything.

cases.name: storage unavailable
cases.why: THE BATCH WAS NOT STORED. An SDK that treats 503 as success loses data. Retry-After is the floor of an exponential schedule, so an outage of minutes does not use up the retry budget in seconds.

cases.name: gateway error
cases.why: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped, then drop and record a send_error outcome.

cases.name: network failure or timeout
cases.why: A timed-out request whose response never arrived is a failure even if the server stored it: event_id makes the resend safe.
